monuments.name: Taj Mahal
facts: Built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal
Construction began in 1632 and took 22 years to complete
Made of white marble with intricate inlay work
One of the Seven Wonders of the World
UNESCO World Heritage Site

stories.romantic: The Taj Mahal stands as an eternal symbol of love! Emperor Shah Jahan was so heartbroken by his wife's death that he built this magnificent monument to honor her memory. Imagine - 22 years of dedication, thousands of artisans, all for love!
stories.historical: Construction of the Taj Mahal began in 1632. Over 20,000 workers and 1,000 elephants were employed to transport materials. The main architect was Ustad Ahmad Lahauri, and the project cost an estimated 32 million rupees at that time.
stories.architectural: The Taj Mahal is a masterpiece of Mughal architecture, combining elements from Persian, Ottoman Turkish, and Indian architectural styles. The white marble changes color throughout the day - pink in the morning, milky white in the evening, and golden under moonlight!

monuments.name: Red Fort
facts: Built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1648
Served as the main residence of Mughal emperors for 200 years
Made of red sandstone
Site of India's Independence Day celebrations
UNESCO World Heritage Site

stories.romantic: The Red Fort witnessed countless royal romances and celebrations! Its beautiful gardens and palaces were home to emperors and their families for centuries.
stories.historical: On August 15, 1947, India's first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru raised the Indian flag here, marking India's independence. Every year since, the Prime Minister addresses the nation from its ramparts!
stories.architectural: The fort's massive red sandstone walls stretch for 2.5 kilometers! Inside, you'll find stunning palaces like Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience) and Diwan-i-Khas (Hall of Private Audience), where the famous Peacock Throne once stood.

monuments.name: Gateway of India
facts: Built to commemorate the visit of King George V and Queen Mary in 1911
Completed in 1924
Built in Indo-Saracenic style
Overlooks the Arabian Sea
Mumbai's most iconic landmark

stories.romantic: The Gateway of India has been the backdrop for countless love stories! Couples gather here to watch the sunset over the Arabian Sea, creating magical moments.
stories.historical: Ironically, this monument built to welcome British royalty also witnessed their departure! The last British troops left India through this very gateway in 1948, symbolizing the end of colonial rule.
stories.architectural: Standing 26 meters tall, this magnificent arch combines Hindu and Muslim architectural styles. The central dome is inspired by 16th-century Gujarati architecture, while the archway reflects Islamic influences!

monuments.name: Qutub Minar
facts: Tallest brick minaret in the world at 73 meters
Construction started in 1192 by Qutb ud-Din Aibak
Completed by his successor Iltutmish
Made of red sandstone and marble
UNESCO World Heritage Site

stories.romantic: Legend says the tower was built as a victory monument, but some believe it was also meant to call the faithful to prayer, spreading love and devotion across the land!
stories.historical: Qutub Minar marks the beginning of Muslim rule in India. It was built using materials from 27 Hindu and Jain temples, symbolizing the transition of power in medieval India.
stories.architectural: The tower has five distinct stories, each marked by a projecting balcony. The first three stories are made of red sandstone, while the fourth and fifth are of marble and sandstone. It tapers from 15 meters at the base to just 2.5 meters at the top!

monuments.name: Hawa Mahal
facts: Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh
Has 953 small windows called jharokhas
Built in the form of Lord Krishna's crown
Made of red and pink sandstone
Part of Jaipur's City Palace complex

stories.romantic: The 'Palace of Winds' was built so royal ladies could observe street festivals and daily life without being seen! These 953 windows allowed cool breezes to flow through, keeping the palace comfortable even in Rajasthan's scorching heat.
stories.historical: Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh built this architectural marvel as an extension of the Royal City Palace. It allowed royal women to practice 'purdah' while still enjoying the vibrant street life of Jaipur.
stories.architectural: Despite its grand five-story facade, Hawa Mahal is only one room deep! The honeycomb structure with its 953 windows creates a stunning visual effect and serves as a natural air conditioning system. The pink sandstone gives it a warm, welcoming glow!
